title: Cheaper turns: a fast gate and scripts instead of bookkeeping

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

items.title: The suite's slowest file stops rebuilding its world per test
items.what: tests/test_warmup.py builds a git repo plus three bin/tracker subprocesses in every test's setUp: 574.9s for 122 tests (finding 23/F-06). Build the seeded project once and copytree it per test. No assertion changes.
items.done: test_warmup's wall clock measured before and after on the same commit, with an unchanged `Ran N tests` line.

parts.title: Build the seeded project once, copy it per test

items.title: The merge gate runs the parallel runner that already exists
items.what: bin/quiet --jobs was built for 23/M-01 and never wired in (finding 23/F-07). Shards dispatch longest-known-first from a duration cache, --jobs auto resolves to cpu_count()-2, and .common-rules.json's gates.merge plus bin/land pass it.
items.done: Serial vs --jobs auto wall clock measured on the same commit after O-01; gates.merge and bin/land use it; the verdict line's shape is unchanged.

items.title: No waiting on a gate: one blocking call, one verdict line
items.what: An agent that backgrounds a gate and polls it spends a full context re-send (~134k tokens, measured) per check to learn nothing. The standard says: run the gate in the foreground, read the verdict line in the same turn, never park a turn on a timer. Mandatory Standard change, in the brief template, the lead prompt and CLAUDE-workflow.md.
items.done: A Standard change (mandatory) CHANGELOG entry; the rule in templates/brief.md, templates/lead-prompt.md and CLAUDE-workflow.md; a test that fails if the brief template loses it.

items.title: bin/commit-if-green: gate, verdict and commit in one call
items.what: Today a builder reads the gate's verdict, then issues git add, git commit and git push as separate tool calls -- four model turns for a mechanical sequence, and the OK/FAILED check is applied by the model rather than by code. One wrapper runs the gate, commits and pushes only on a verdict line matching ^OK with no ^FAILED, and reports what it did.
items.done: Refuses on FAILED, on a non-zero exit and on an empty verdict; commits nothing in either case; tested against a fixture repo with a passing and a failing gate.

items.title: A PR body drafted from the ledger item and the diff
items.what: The lead composes every PR title and body from memory of the item and the diff, having already read both. A script prints a skeleton -- item id, title, files touched, test counts -- for the lead to edit rather than compose.
items.done: Prints a usable body for a real branch and item; the lead's edits are what lands; tested on a fixture ledger and diff.

items.title: One draft for the ruflo-item done note and the ledger event
items.what: The same facts (item id, commit, PR, test counts) are written twice by hand: once as the ruflo-item done summary, once as tracker set --event text. Draft both from the same source; the lead adjusts wording.
items.done: Both texts drafted from one call on a fixture item; the lead's wording still wins; tested.

items.title: Batch dispatch: one message carries every unblocked brief
items.what: Six briefs in one message cost one lead turn; six messages cost six. The standard already says to spawn every unblocked C1/C2 item in one message -- say it as a cost rule, with the same rule for reviewing branches, and say that a lead never sends a brief a turn at a time.
items.done: Standard change (mandatory) entry; the rule in the lead prompt and CLAUDE-workflow.md; a test pinning it in the templates.
